mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: The greatest threat for severe hail/wind in the short term should focus across a small part of south-central North Dakota, including the Bismarck area

details.label: Summary
details.text: The greatest threat for severe hail/wind in the short term should focus across a small part of south-central North Dakota, including the Bismarck area

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A cluster of supercells is ongoing as of 0330Z across south-central ND, aided by a weak mid-level disturbance moving southeastward across the northern Plains. Given favorable deep-layer shear and enhanced (40-50+ kt) westerly flow at 6+ km AGL shown on the latest VWP from KBIS, this activity will likely maintain organization in the near term. Severe hail and damaging winds may occur, with strong inbound velocities approaching the Bismarck area on latest radar imagery. Very large hail up to 2 inches in diameter has recently been reported with the strongest core. Longer-term prospects for these supercells remain uncertain, as weaker instability and stronger MLCIN are present with eastward/southward extent into southeast ND and northern SD

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...55-70 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...1.50-2.50 IN

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Percolating cumulus is being monitored for deep convective initiation across central Wisconsin. While it is unclear if thunderstorms will develop, the regional environment is conditionally supportive of strong/severe thunderstorms

details.label: Summary
details.text: Percolating cumulus is being monitored for deep convective initiation across central Wisconsin. While it is unclear if thunderstorms will develop, the regional environment is conditionally supportive of strong/severe thunderstorms

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Over the past 30 minutes, deepening cumulus has been noted in GOES IR imagery along a surface trough/confluence zone across central WI. Earlier attempts at convective initiation have been noted further west across southeast MN and western WI as a subtle mid-level wave traverses northern IA. It is unclear if this more recent development is associated with this mid-level feature or weak ascent along the confluence zone (or a combination of both). Regardless, the recent 00 UTC MPX sounding sampled rich low-level moisture on the warm side of the boundary, and steep mid-level lapse rates with MLCAPE values just under 3000 J/kg. Accounting for drier and cooler conditions across WI suggests that buoyancy is somewhat more limited, but still supportive of deep convection. Additionally, 50 knot flow aloft coupled with weak low-level winds hints that hodographs will be sufficiently elongated to support organized convection, including the potential for supercells. Despite the conditionally supportive environment, it is unclear if ascent will be sufficient to initiate and sustain deep convection. Earlier failed attempts suggest ascent is too meager, and recent HRRR/RRFS solutions have been trending towards more limited thunderstorm coverage with successive runs. Consequently, confidence in a robust/widespread severe threat is limited. Nonetheless, convective trends will continue to be monitored given the number of candidate updrafts emerging in IR imagery

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...UP TO 60 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...1.00-1.75 IN
